thread:
maria.g: 🚨 heads-up: hosted-us-east GPU pool is showing sustained saturation. 4/5 nodes at 98% GPU util, queue length ~850, admission control kicking in returning 429s to some customers. alert: GPU_POOL_SATURATION_us-east-1 at 1772034565.
kevin.l: seeing the same on the dashboard — spikes started ~10:12 UTC. any known deploys?
ops-bot: [ALERT] GPU_POOL_SATURATION_us-east-1 triggered by policy 'queued_requests>600' (severity: high). Pager notified.
sre-oncall: I have the pool logs open. attaching quick tail of scheduler logs: 
```
2026-03-18T10:12:34Z scheduler: queue_length=623 pool=hosted-us-east-1
2026-03-18T10:13:02Z admission: rejecting request user=acct-123 status=429
2026-03-18T10:14:10Z autoscaler: scale_event failed: capacity_limit_reached
```
kevin.l: hmm autoscaler failed because quota cap hit for hosted capacity? getting 'quota exceeded' in autoscaler trace.
anika: can we roll traffic to us-west-2 as a short-term fallback? manifest routing has region-fallback but not auto for hosted tier.
maria.g: yes, but need to check data residency for some customers. for public customers we can route.
ryan.k: cost note — spinning up extra on-demand GPUs in us-east will be ~$4k/day. Routing to us-west-2 will add ~15-40ms tail latency for some customers but saves immediate cost.
kevin.l: quick mitigation options: 1) enable routing fallback for non-PII tenants to us-west-2, 2) temporarily bump admission control per-tenant for internal/whitelisted accounts, 3) drop lower-priority batch jobs.
sre-oncall: implementing option 3 now — pausing scheduled quantize/export jobs that were queued. patching admission rules to deprioritize batch-exports.
anika: I'm enabling fallback routing for public tenants (devex-bot will announce). any objections?
devex-bot: announcing: "Fallback routing enabled for public tenants from hosted-us-east -> hosted-us-west-2. Expect increased latencies for routed requests."
kevin.l: also flagged a noisy customer doing repeated long-context runs — working with account owner to throttle.
maria.g: keeping alerts loud until queue <200 and admission errors stop. will update in 15. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: [UPDATE] queue_length=312 pool=hosted-us-east-1 at 1772034910.
ryan.k: if queue doesn't drop under 200 in 30m we should provision 1 reserved GPU node as emergency and then evaluate cost/rollback.
anika: noted. planning a post-incident RCA focused on: autoscaler quota handling, regional fallback automation, and per-tenant admission policies.
sre-oncall: thanks team — I'll leave monitoring on and escalate if anything regresses.
maria.g: tl;dr mitigations applied: paused noisy batch jobs, enabled public fallback routing, whitelisted internal accounts, notified impacted customers. follow-ups: RCA + playbook updates.
